sentences.text: This small dinosaur measured 1.7 meters in length and had a mass of approximately 25 kilograms.
Scientists know the animal from one nearly complete skeleton containing a full skull, lower jaw, and partial limbs.
Its head bore a distinctive casque similar to that of a cassowary, built from many bones absent in related species.
Unlike its relative Oviraptor, the skeleton of this creature was constructed more lightly and lacked robustness.
A nearly complete skeleton was unearthed in 1984 at the Altan Uul II locality within the Gobi Desert.
Rinchen Barsbold first described the specimen as Oviraptor mongoliensis in 1986.
He later assigned the fossil to the new genus Rinchenia in 1997.
The genus name honors Byambyn Rinchen, the father of the paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold.
The specific name mongoliensis indicates the region where the holotype was discovered.
The genus Rinchenia was originally established by Barsbold in 1997.
It is classified within the family Oviraptoridae.
However, the genus authority is now attributed to Osmólska and colleagues in 2004.
This animal lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Mongolia.
It inhabited the environment approximately 70 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
Some evidence suggests it also lived during the Maastrichtian stage, spanning from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
A reexamination found differences significant enough to warrant separating Rinchenia from Oviraptor into its own genus.
